## Keep the product fixed

List pairs in order of increasing absolute value of the first number. Compare each sum with the target.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$x^2+8x+12$

::: {.fragment}

**P** $=12$, **S** $=8$. Both signs are positive.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Signed pair | Sum |
|:--|:--|
| $1,\ 12$ | $13$ |
| $2,\ 6$ | $8$ |
| $3,\ 4$ | $7$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

**F:** Select $2,6$: $2+6=8$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$x^2+8x+12=(x+2)(x+6)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$x^2-8x+12$

Predict the signs. List the pairs, circle your choice and factorise.

:::

::: {.fragment}

**P** $=12$, **S** $=-8$. Both signs are negative.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Signed pair | Sum |
|:--|:--|
| $-1,\ -12$ | $-13$ |
| $-2,\ -6$ | $-8$ |
| $-3,\ -4$ | $-7$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

**F:** Select $-2,-6$: $-2-6=-8$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$x^2-8x+12=(x-2)(x-6)$

:::

:::::

::::::
